paper_title: Network-based machine learning in colorectal and bladder organoid models predicts anti-cancer drug efficacy in patients
prediction_task: Anti-cancer drug response prediction from network-based transcriptomic signatures in organoid models

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Analytical approach is outdated and simplistic — many publications already describe similar strategies with much more advanced deep learning methods. Authors must show (i) PPI-guided selection beats unguided penalized regression, (ii) drug-target proximity beats random pathway selection, (iii) organoid data beats large-scale cell line screens (GDSC/CCLE), (iv) method works better than existing network-guided regression.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added comprehensive comparisons with GDSC, random pathway controls, and deep learning baselines.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Results from a unique drug response prediction don't look convincing. Should perform validation using much more comprehensive pharmacogenomics datasets encompassing thousands of observations across hundreds of compounds.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added pan-drug validation across GDSC and CCLE.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Authors do not account for biases from reference network topology — over-characterized genes with more connections will always be 'proximal'. Need proper randomization to estimate this bias.

reviewer_strengths.text: Tackles a critical and timely problem. Assembling models from public preclinical data for personalized medicine is of paramount importance.
